transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Lately I can’t seem to focus on my analyses at work—my mind keeps going blank even when I’m staring right at the spreadsheets. It's gotten to the point where I'm really struggling to get through my daily tasks, so I decided I needed to seek some help.
Did these concentration problems start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without any clear trigger? If there was a stressor, what was it?

It really started about fifteen months ago when I was promoted into a much higher-visibility role at work. I suddenly had to juggle multiple client accounts, tight deadlines, and frequent late-night calls with overseas teams. The pressure just kept escalating until I felt completely overwhelmed, and that's when my concentration really started to slip.
Along with the concentration problems, have you been feeling down most days or losing interest in things you usually enjoy? If so, has that lasted for at least two weeks?

I wouldn't say I feel depressed or down, but I've definitely stopped doing things I enjoy because I'm just too wired and anxious. I'm constantly worrying about work, which makes it impossible to relax or actually enjoy hanging out with my friends anymore.

If your work pressure eased or you took time away, would the anxiety and concentration problems mostly improve, or do they continue even when you're not dealing with that stress? Have these symptoms stayed present for most of the 15 months?

They definitely persist even when I'm away from work; even on weekends or trips, my mind constantly wanders to worst-case scenarios, and I worry about non-work things like whether I locked my apartment door. This has been a constant, daily struggle ever since I started the new role fifteen months ago, without any real let-up.

If your job demands were removed or you changed to a less stressful role, do you think the worry would still continue across different areas of your life? Or does it feel mainly tied to that work promotion and the stress that came with it?

Although the promotion definitely triggered everything, the worry now feels like it has taken on a life of its own and would likely continue even if my job changed. It has spilled over into daily life, making me obsess over minor things like whether I locked my apartment door, and I can't seem to stop the "what if" thoughts even when I'm just trying to relax and watch a show.

Along with the constant worry, have you also had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or feeling irritable? If so, which ones have been present most days?

I definitely struggle with terrible sleep and extreme fatigue; I lie awake until 2 or 3 a.m. replaying work scenarios and wake up constantly. Even on weekends, I feel completely exhausted, like I'm dragging my body through molasses, and I just feel constantly tense and wired.

When the worry starts, do you feel able to control or stop it, or does it keep going despite your efforts? Also, have you been feeling especially restless/on edge or more irritable than usual on most days?

The worry feels completely uncontrollable—I’ll try to distract myself with a book or a show, but within minutes the "what if" thoughts sneak back in and snowball. As for being on edge, I wouldn't say I'm irritable, but I feel constantly wired, tense, and completely unable to relax.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes excessive, difficult-to-control worry occurring daily for 15 months across multiple domains beyond the original work trigger, with associated concentration difficulty, sleep disturbance, fatigue, and persistent tension/restlessness causing clear occupational and social impairment. This pattern is most consistent with generalized anxiety disorder rather than a transient stress reaction or depressive disorder.
